decisions.reason: In raw_data.csv (line 324), the primary student report for metaxa-kakavouli2018 (Metaxa-Kakavouli et al., 2018, Study 1) is not included in the source archive (replication_report_included = no). Although raw_data.csv lists t(108) = 3.47 for the original (N = 110) and t(50) = 2.68 in the same direction for the replication (N = 98), it notes that 'the df for student's t-test is quite possibly wrong, but can't tell' and assigns fractional subjective scores of 0.5 (instructor) and 0.5 (report). As Boyce et al. (2023, line 92) state, fractional values on the 0-1 scale 'reflected the raters’ uncertainty where available evidence was hard to interpret.' Without the primary report in the source text, it is impossible to determine whether the 0.5 rating reflects a genuinely mixed outcome across multiple measures/sub-tests, rater uncertainty due to the questionable degrees of freedom, or a successful focal contrast qualified by secondary caveats.

decisions.quote: Discussion Summary of Replication Attempt The original study reported a significant difference in affect ratings between the two conditions, such that affect toward Asian Americans was significantly more negative in the realistic threat condition (partner: Jamal, M = 62.11, SD = 22.91) than in the no realistic threat condition (partner: Yoshi, M = 78.57, SD = 17.90), F(1, 39) = 6.48, p = .015, η2 = .015. I was able to fully replicate the significance of this difference, but the finding is not as robust as the original, as reflected in the weaker evidence shown in the p values and F values.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding record the replication of Maddux et al. (2008) Study 3 as 'successful' (flagged only because the shipped quote used synthetic boilerplate). In the included primary replication report (maddux2008.html, line 636) and raw_data.csv (line 234), the pre-registered confirmatory analysis on affect ratings toward Asian Americans significantly replicated the original effect in the same direction (realistic threat M = 71.2, SD = 17.4 vs. no realistic threat M = 79.9, SD = 17.5, F(1, 76) = 4.779, p = .032; original M = 62.11, SD = 22.91 vs. M = 78.57, SD = 17.90, F(1, 39) = 6.48, p = .015), with the author concluding 'I was able to fully replicate the significance of this difference' and both instructor and report codes equal to 1 (a secondary non-significant test on attitude was explicitly designated as an exploratory analysis rather than the key target finding).
